page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v6 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the 5th Generation Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with a peak clock frequency of 4.2 GHz, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX-Tile, and AMX-INT8. Memory is configured at 384 GB, adhering to a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Local ephemeral storage is bundled via a 5,669 GB NVMe SSD, delivering high-speed scratch space directly to the host without reliance on network-attached volumes.

Benchmark results place the D96ds_v6 in the top tier for multi-core compute performance, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 21,967 and PassMark CPU reaching 86,698.13. Vectorized and accelerated workloads benefit substantially from integrated AMX instructions, reflected in a PassMark CPU extended instructions score of 105,443.81. Data-handling metrics are consistently strong, demonstrating 107.53 million Redis SET operations per second, PassMark database throughput of 32,248.97, and top-tier static web serving throughput of 116.39 GB/sec. LLM prompt ingestion tests also register strong throughput due to high memory bandwidth and AMX matrix acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D96ds_v6 packages dense multi-core processing with substantial bundled NVMe capacity, eliminating the need for premium provisioned IOPS disks for high-IOPS temporary caching and intermediate data stages. The lack of a discrete GPU limits its efficiency for large-scale deep learning model inference generation, where tokens per second scale down significantly relative to dedicated accelerators. However, for CPU-bound computational pipelines, the inclusion of dedicated physical execution threads minimizes performance jitter.

This server type fits high-concurrency production workloads requiring balanced compute and memory along with rapid local data retrieval. Typical deployment targets include large relational and NoSQL databases, Redis distributed caching tiers, extensive Clang software compilation pipelines, web application serving arrays, and batch analytics processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Intel Xeon 8573C processor using the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs operating at speeds up to 4.2 GHz, it pairs 384 GB of RAM with 5,669 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results in multi-core compute, static web serving throughput, and extended instruction execution, bolstered by hardware-level AMX and AVX-512 support. The platform demonstrates strong performance across database operations, multi-threaded decompression, and in-memory caching with Redis. While large-model LLM generation throughput remains modest compared to GPU-accelerated instances, the dense core allocation and fast bundled local disk offer solid resource density. The instance is suited for enterprise database hosting, large-scale CI/CD build environments, and high-concurrency web services.
